body.translated_text: <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s> (Verses on the Accumulation of Precious Qualities)

children.text: 1 atha khalu bhagavāṃstāsāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ saṃpraharṣaṇārthaṃ punarapīmāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ paridīpayamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
children.translated_text: 1. Then the Blessed One, in order to delight those four assemblies, illuminating this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> once more, at that time spoke these verses:
Having established supreme love, reverence, and faith,
Having abandoned obscurations, gone beyond the stains of afflictions,
Listen! [To the teaching] of those who have set forth for the world's welfare, of excellent vows—
The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), where the heroes practice.
As many rivers as flow here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>,
Producing fruits, flowers, medicines, and forest trees—
They arise from the power of the king of <s>Nāgas</s>, the lord of elephants,
Such is the majestic splendor of that lord of the world.
As many teachings as the hearers of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) teach,
Speak, and proclaim together with reasoning,
The creation of supreme bliss and the attainment of its fruit—
All this is the work of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ya jina bhāṣati dharmanetrīṃ
children.translated_text: For what reason does the <s>Jina</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s>-guide?
Those trained therein, who have become disciples of the bull among men,
Having realized [it] directly, teach as they were trained—
Is this the <s>Buddha</s>'s power, or the power of their own strength?
Where there is no apprehension of the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
No apprehension of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, nor of the mind, nor of awakening—

children.text: evaṃ śruṇitva na ca muhyati nāsti trāso
children.translated_text: One who, hearing thus, is neither bewildered nor afraid,
That <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices the wisdom of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones).

children.text: na ca rupa vedana na saṃjña na cetanā ca
children.translated_text: Neither form, nor feeling, nor perception, nor volition,

children.text: vijñāna sthānu aṇumātra na bhonti tasya
children.translated_text: Nor consciousness exists for him, even in the slightest atomic measure—
Established in no <s>dharma</s>, wandering without a home,
Without grasping, he attains the awakening of the <s>Sugatas</s>.
And as for the wanderer <s>Śreṇika</s>'s understanding—
There is no apprehension of knowledge, nor analysis of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates)—
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who thoroughly knows <s>dharmas</s> in this way

children.text: na ca nirvṛtiṃ spṛśati so viharāti prajñām
children.translated_text: Does not touch <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation); he abides in wisdom.
And further, he investigates: in which [<s>dharmas</s>] is wisdom?

children.text: kasmātkuto va imi śūnyaka sarva dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: From what, from where are all these <s>dharmas</s> empty?

children.text: vyuparīkṣamāṇu na ca līyati nāsti trāso
children.translated_text: Investigating thus, he does not shrink back nor is there fear—
That <s>Bodhisattva</s> is near to <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

children.text: saci rupa saṃjña api vedana cetanā ca
children.translated_text: If he practices in form, perception, feeling, and volition,
In the aggregate of consciousness, without truly knowing [them]—
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who conceptualizes these aggregates as empty
Practices unattached, in the stage of non-grasping at signs.

children.text: na ca rupa vedana na saṃjña na cetanāyā
children.translated_text: One who does not practice in form, feeling, perception, volition,
Or consciousness—wandering without a home—
That wisdom-bearer does not conceive that he practices—
Without grasping, he touches the supreme tranquil <s>samādhi</s>.
Thus abiding in self-tranquility, this <s>Bodhisattva</s>
Was predicted [to <s>bodhi</s>] by former <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.text: na ca manyate ahu samādhitu vyutthito vā
children.translated_text: Yet he does not think: I have emerged from <s>samādhi</s>,
Because he has thoroughly understood the nature of <s>dharmas</s>.
Practicing thus, he practices the wisdom of the <s>Sugatas</s>,

children.text: no cāpi so labhati yatra carāti dharmam
children.translated_text: Yet he does not find the <s>dharma</s> in which he practices.
Having understood that practice is also non-practice,
This is the practice of the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: yo 'sau na vidyati sa eṣa avidyamāno
children.translated_text: That which does not exist—this very non-existent [thing],

children.text: tāṃ bālu kalpayi avidya karoti vidyām
children.translated_text: The fool conceptualizes, making ignorance into knowledge.

children.text: vidyā avidya ubhi eti asanta dharmā
children.translated_text: Knowledge and ignorance, both are unreal <s>dharmas</s>—
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who understands thus transcends.

children.text: māyopamāṃ ya iha jānati pañca skandhāṃ
children.translated_text: One who here knows the five <s>skandhas</s> as illusion-like

children.text: na ca māya anya na ca skandha karoti anyān
children.translated_text: Does not make illusion one thing and the <s>skandhas</s> another.
Free from the perception of multiplicity, practicing in peace,
This is the practice of the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
For one who possesses a good spiritual friend and is endowed with insight,

children.text: trāso na bheṣyati śruṇitva jināna mātrām
children.translated_text: There will be no fear upon hearing the <s>Jinas</s>' mother (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>).
But one who has a bad spiritual friend and is led by others
Is like a raw vessel—split when touched by water.
For what reason is this one called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>?
Wishing to cut off attachment everywhere while still creating engagement,
He will touch the <s>bodhi</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>, which is free from attachment—
Therefore he receives the name <s>Bodhisattva</s>.
<s>Mahāsattva</s> (Great Being)—for what reason is he so called?
He will be great here for the vast host of beings.
He cuts the great [net of] views of the host of beings—
For this reason he is called <s>Mahāsattva</s>.
A great leader, of great wisdom, of great power,
Mounted on the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), the supreme <s>samādhi</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>—
Armored with greatness: I shall challenge the deceiver <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>)!
For this reason he is called <s>Mahāsattva</s>.
Just as a magician, having conjured at a crossroads,
Cuts off many hundreds of thousands of heads of a great crowd—

children.text: yatha te ca māya tatha jānati sarvasattvāṃ
children.translated_text: He knows all beings as he knows that illusion;

children.text: nirmāṇu sarva jagato na ca tasya trāso
children.translated_text: As to the conjuring of the whole world, there is no fear for him.

children.text: rupaṃ ca saṃjña api vedana cetanā ca
children.translated_text: Form, perception, feeling, and volition,

children.text: vijñāna bandhu na ca mukta asaṅgabhūto
children.translated_text: And consciousness—neither bound nor liberated, free from attachment—

children.text: evaṃ ca bodhi kramate na ca līnacitto
children.translated_text: Thus he advances toward <s>bodhi</s> without a shrinking mind.
This is the armor of the foremost, supreme persons.
For what reason is this one called one whose vehicle is <s>bodhi</s>?
Having mounted it, he brings all beings to <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
This vehicle, the great palace, is equal to space—
The supreme vehicle that conveys to happiness, bliss, and safety.

children.text: na ca labhyate ya vrajate diśa āruhitvā
children.translated_text: That which, having mounted and traveled in every direction, is not found—
The going to the abode of <s>nirvāṇa</s>—there is no destination to apprehend.

children.text: yatha agni nirvṛtu na tasya gatipracāro
children.translated_text: Just as an extinguished fire has no course of going—
For this reason it is called <s>nirvṛti</s> (extinction).
A <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not apprehended in the past,
Nor in the future, nor in the present—pure in the three times.
What is pure is unconditioned, free from conceptual elaboration—
This is the practice of the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: yasmiṃś ca kāli samaye vidu bodhisattvo
children.translated_text: At whatever time and occasion the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>,
Practicing thus, reflects without grasping,

children.text: mahatīṃ janeti karuṇāṃ na ca sattvasaṃjñā
children.translated_text: Generates great compassion yet without the perception of beings—
This is the practice of the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
If, taking up the perception of beings and the perception of suffering,
[He thinks] I shall remove suffering and accomplish welfare for the world—
That <s>Bodhisattva</s> who conceptualizes self and beings
Does not practice the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
As he knows himself, so he knows all beings;
As [he knows] all beings, so he knows all <s>dharmas</s>—
Not conceptualizing in terms of either grasping or non-grasping,
This is the practice of the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
As many <s>dharma</s>-names as are proclaimed in the world—
Having transcended and departed from attachment to all of them,

children.text: amṛtaṃ ti jñānu paramaṃ na tu yo pareṇa
children.translated_text: That supreme knowledge is called the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>), not surpassed by another—
It is one in meaning with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection).

children.text: evaṃ carantu na ca kāṅkṣati bodhisattvo
children.translated_text: Practicing thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not doubt.

children.text: jñātavya yo vihara te sa upāyaprajño
children.translated_text: One who is to be known abides—he is skillful in means and wisdom.
Knowing that <s>dharmas</s> are by nature unreal—
This is the practice of the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the first chapter, named The Practice of Omniscience (<s>Sarvākārajñatācaryāparivarta</s>).

children.text: rupasmi yo na sthihate na ca vedanāyāṃ
children.translated_text: One who does not stand in form, nor in feeling,

children.text: saṃjñāya yo na sthihate na ca cetanāyām
children.translated_text: Who does not stand in perception, nor in volition,

children.text: vijñāni yo na sthihate sthitu dharmatāyāṃ
children.translated_text: Who does not stand in consciousness but stands in the nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>)—
This is the practice of the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Permanent and impermanent, pleasant and suffering, pure and impure,
Self and non-self, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),
Standing in the attainment of the fruit, in the stage of an <s>Arhat</s>,
Standing in the stage of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, likewise in the stage of a <s>Buddha</s>—
Just as the Guide does not stand in the unconditioned element (<s>dhātu</s>),
So too standing in the conditioned, he wanders without a home.

children.text: evaṃ ca sthānu athito sthita bodhisattvo
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stands in standing [that is] non-standing—

children.text: asthānu sthānu ayu sthānu jinena ukto
children.translated_text: Non-standing is standing: this standing was declared by the <s>Jina</s>.
If one wishes: May I become a hearer of the <s>Sugata</s>,
Or a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, or a king of <s>Dharma</s>—
One cannot attain this patient acceptance of the non-arising [of <s>dharmas</s>]
Without seeing the farther shore, like [crossing] from this bank to the far bank.

children.text: yo dharma bhāṣyati ya bhāṣyati bhāṣyamāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: The one who teaches <s>Dharma</s>, the one who teaches [to] those being taught,
The fruit-attainer, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and the Lord of the World—
<s>Nirvāṇa</s>, as understood by the wise and learned—
All these are the self-born [offspring], as pointed out by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: catvāri pudgala ime na trasanti ye 'smin
children.translated_text: These four persons do not tremble in this [teaching]:
The son of the <s>Jina</s>, one skilled in truth, the irreversible one,
The <s>Arhat</s> whose stains and afflictions are shaken off and whose doubts are abandoned,
And fourthly, one who has been matured by a good spiritual friend.
Practicing thus, the wise, learned <s>Bodhisattva</s>
Does not train in the stage of an <s>Arhat</s>, nor in the stage of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>,
But trains in the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> for the sake of omniscience.

children.text: śikṣāaśikṣa na ya śikṣati eṣa śikṣā
children.translated_text: Training that is non-training—that is the [true] training.
Not for the purpose of grasping the increase or decrease of form,
Nor does he train for the purpose of grasping various <s>dharmas</s>—
But training, he grasps omniscience.

children.text: niryāyatī ya iya śikṣa guṇe ratānām
children.translated_text: This is the going forth—this training—of those who delight in virtues.

children.text: rupe na prajña iti rupi na asti prajñā
children.translated_text: Wisdom is not in form; nor is there wisdom in the formful;

children.text: vijñāna saṃjña api vedana cetanā ca
children.translated_text: Consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition—

children.text: na ca eti prajña iti teṣa na asti prajñā
children.translated_text: Wisdom does not go to them, nor is there wisdom in them.
Like the element of space, there is no division of it.
The nature of objects is endless and boundless;

children.text: sattvāna yā ca prakṛtī sa anantapārā
children.translated_text: The nature of beings is likewise endless and boundless;
The nature of the element of space is endless and boundless;
The wisdom of the knowers of the world is also endless and boundless.
Perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>)—this name was proclaimed by the Guide;
Having discerned perception, they go to the farther shore through its abandonment.
Those who attain the cessation of perception therein

children.text: te pāraprāpta sthita pāramite hu bhonti
children.translated_text: Are those who have reached the farther shore, established in the <s>Pāramitā</s>.
Even if this Guide were to proclaim the word being for <s>kalpas</s>
Equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
Where would the arising of a being come from, [since it is] pure from the beginning?
This is the practice of the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Thus the <s>Jina</s> speaks, one who speaks without contradiction:
When I practiced this noble <s>Pāramitā</s>,
Then I was predicted by the supreme Person above all:
You shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in a future age.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the second chapter, named The Chapter on <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Śakraparivarta</s>).

children.text: ya imāṃ grahīṣyati paryāpuṇatī sa nityaṃ
children.translated_text: One who will take up and master this
<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, where the Protectors practice—

children.text: viṣa vahni śastra udakaṃ na kramāti tasyo
children.translated_text: Poison, fire, weapons, and water will not overcome him,

children.text: otāru māru na ca vindati mārapakṣo
children.translated_text: And <s>Māra</s> and the forces of <s>Māra</s> will find no entry.
If someone were to build <s>stūpas</s> for the <s>Sugata</s> who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,
And worship [them] with the seven treasures for an entire age—
And with these fill thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of world-realms,
With <s>stūpas</s> of the <s>Sugata</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>—
And as many beings as [there are] in those <s>koṭis</s> of realms
Were all to make offerings for endless <s>kalpas</s>
With divine flowers, excellent fragrances, and unguents
For <s>kalpas</s> conceived as the three times and even more—
Yet one who writes this Mother of the <s>Sugatas</s> in a book,
From which the Leaders, the Ten-Powered Ones, arise,
And holds it, honors it with flowers and unguents—

children.text: kala puṇya bhonti na sa stūpi karitva pūjām
children.translated_text: The merit from the <s>stūpa</s>-building and worship would be [only] a fraction [of this].
The great <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), wisdom, this <s>Pāramitā</s> of beings,
Allaying suffering, <s>dharma</s>-sorrow, and grief for the vast host of beings—
Those who are past and those who are Lords of the World in the ten directions,
Trained in this <s>vidyā</s>, [they became] supreme kings of physicians.
Those who practice the conduct of benevolence and compassion,
Trained in this <s>vidyā</s>, the wise shall touch <s>bodhi</s>.

children.text: ye saukhya saṃskṛta asaṃskṛta ye ca saukhyā
children.translated_text: Whatever happiness is conditioned and whatever happiness is unconditioned—

children.text: sarve ca saukhya prasutā itu veditavyāḥ
children.translated_text: All happiness is to be known as born from this.
Seeds scattered on the earth come into being;
Having obtained the conditions, they grow into many forms.
As many qualities of <s>bodhi</s> and the five <s>pāramitās</s> as there are—
They all grow from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: yenaiva rāja vrajate sa ha cakravartī
children.translated_text: Wherever the <s>Cakravartin</s> king goes,
There go the seven treasures and all the armies.
Wherever this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>Jinas</s> goes,
There all qualities and <s>dharmas</s> come together.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the third chapter, named Immeasurable Qualities, Holding the <s>Pāramitā</s>, and Veneration of <s>Stūpas</s>.
<s>Śakra</s>, questioned by the <s>Jina</s>, spoke [this] question:
If there were <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
All filled with relics of the <s>Jina</s>, bound into <s>cūḍā</s>-shrines—
This very excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) they grasp.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ na mi śarīri agauravatvaṃ
children.translated_text: For what reason is there no disrespect toward my bodily form?
Rather, indeed, those cultivated by wisdom worship it.

children.text: yatha rājaniśrita naro labhi sarvi pūjāṃ
children.translated_text: Just as a man dependent on a king obtains all honor,
So too the <s>buddhadhātu</s> (buddha-nature) dependent on <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
A jewel-gem endowed with all qualities, priceless—
The casket in which it resides is worthy of reverence.
Even when it is removed, they still desire the casket,
For those qualities belong to that great jewel.
Just so, the qualities of the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—
Even when the <s>Jina</s> has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the relics receive worship.
Therefore, one who desires to obtain those qualities of the <s>Jina</s>
Should grasp the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—this is liberation.
Let wisdom be the forerunner when giving <s>dāna</s> (generosity),

children.text: śīle ca kṣānti tatha vīrya tathaiva dhyāne
children.translated_text: In <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), and likewise <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
She encompasses and prevents the loss of wholesome dharmas,

children.text: ekā ca sā api nidarśayi sarvadharmān
children.translated_text: And she alone reveals all dharmas.
Just as in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> there are many billions of trees,
Of diverse kinds, varied, and of many forms,
Yet there is no distinction whatsoever among their shadows—
Except when one speaks of the classification by shadow.
Just so, these five <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of the <s>Jinas</s>
Become <s>pāramitās</s> by virtue of the name of <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom).
When all are dedicated to omniscience,
All six converge into one path called <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the fourth chapter called 'Proclamation of Qualities.'

children.text: saci rūpa saṃjña api vedana cetanāyāṃ
children.translated_text: If regarding form, perception, feeling, and volition,
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflects that mind is impermanent and subject to change,
He practices counter-analysis without apprehending—

children.text: na hi dharma paṇḍita vināśa karoti jātu
children.translated_text: For the wise one never causes the destruction of a dharma.

children.text: yasmin na rūpa api vedana cāpi saṃjñā
children.translated_text: Wherein there is neither form, nor feeling, nor perception,
Neither consciousness, nor any apprehension of volition—

children.text: anupādu śūnya na ya jānati sarvadharmān
children.translated_text: Without grasping, empty, one who does not cognize any dharmas—
This is the practice of the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
In as many fields as there are grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
That many beings one might discipline—
Yet one who, having written this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
Gives the book to another being—that one has superior merit.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ta iha śikṣita vādiśreṣṭhā
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because those trained here, the best of speakers,
Lead all dharmas to <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness).

children.text: yāṃ śrutva śrāvaka spṛśanti vimukti śīghraṃ
children.translated_text: Hearing which, <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) quickly attain liberation,
<s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> attain their awakening, and <s>Buddhas</s> attain supreme awakening.
Without a sprout, no tree can arise in the world—
How then could branches, leaves, fruits, and flowers arise?
Without <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), no <s>Jina</s> arises in the world—
How then could the fruits of <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, or the appearance of <s>śrāvakas</s>?
When the orb of the sun releases its net of rays,
Then beings exert themselves in their actions and activities.
Similarly, <s>bodhicitta</s>, ever known to the knower of the world—
Through knowledge, all qualities and dharmas come together.
Just as, without the presence of the great serpent-king,
How could there be flowing rivers here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?
Without rivers, fruits and flowers would not arise,

children.text: na ca sāgarāṇa ratanā bhavi naikarūpāḥ
children.translated_text: Nor would the oceans have their manifold jewels.
Similarly, without the <s>bodhicitta</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
How could there be streams of knowledge in the entire world?

children.text: jñānasya co asati nāsti guṇāna vṛddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Without knowledge, there is no growth of qualities,

children.text: na ca bodhi sāgarasamā na ca buddhadharmāḥ
children.translated_text: Nor <s>bodhi</s> equal to the ocean, nor <s>buddhadharmās</s>.
However many light-bearing beings there are in the world,
All send forth radiance for the purpose of illumination.
Yet a single ray issued from the noble orb of the sun—

children.text: na kalā pi jyotikagaṇe siya sarvaābhāḥ
children.translated_text: All the splendor of the host of lights does not equal even a fraction of it.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the fifth chapter called 'Discourse on Merit.'
However much merit the assemblies of <s>śrāvakas</s> produce,
Through <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), and <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation) combined—
That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a single thought of rejoicing,
Generates a mass of merit not equaled by all the assemblies of <s>śrāvakas</s>.
The billions of <s>Buddhas</s> who have gone before in the past,
And those in endless billions of thousands of fields,
Those who remain and those protectors of the world who have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,
Who teach the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s> for the destruction of suffering—
First, the arising of the excellent thought of awakening,
Up until the time of the cessation of the Dharma of the guides—

children.text: ekasmi tatra ciya teṣa jināna puṇyaṃ
children.translated_text: If one were to gather in one place all the merit of those <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: saha yukta pāramita ye 'pi ca buddhadharmāḥ
children.translated_text: Together with the <s>pāramitās</s> and also the <s>buddhadharmās</s>—
And also of the sons of the <s>Buddhas</s> and of the <s>śrāvakas</s>,
Those in training and those beyond training, wholesome with and without outflows—
Having gathered all this together, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> rejoices,
And dedicates it all to <s>bodhi</s> for the welfare of the world.
If, when dedicating, there persists a perception of mind,
Likewise a perception of 'bodhisattva' in the dedication, and a perception of 'being'—
With mind fixed in perception and view, possessed of three attachments—
Then the dedication does not truly come about when it is apprehended.
If one knows 'it ceases, its nature is destroyed'—
How will they dedicate that which is destroyed?

children.text: na ca dharma dharmi pariṇāmayate kadācit
children.translated_text: Neither a dharma nor a dharma-bearer ever truly dedicates,
Yet dedication does occur for one who truly understands.

children.text: saci so nimitta kurute na ca mānayāti
children.translated_text: If one produces signs but does not regard them with pride,
Then the signless dedication becomes directed toward <s>bodhi</s>.
Just as food mixed with poison, however well-prepared—
So has grasping at wholesome dharmas been declared by the <s>Jina</s>.
Therefore, one should train in proper dedication,

children.text: yatha te jinā kuśala eva prajānayanti
children.translated_text: As the <s>Jinas</s> understand what is truly wholesome.
Whatever its nature, whatever its origin, whatever its signlessness—
'I rejoice thus, and thus I dedicate.'
Thus dedicating merit toward <s>bodhi</s>,

children.text: na ca so hi buddha kṣipate jina uktavādī
children.translated_text: One does not disparage the <s>Buddha</s>—so the <s>Jina</s> has declared.
However many <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the world grasp at things,
The hero who dedicates in this way surpasses them all.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the sixth chapter called 'Rejoicing.'
Billions of the born-blind without a guide—
Ignorant of the path, how could they enter the city?

children.text: vina prajña pañca imi pāramitā acakṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Without wisdom, these five <s>pāramitās</s> are eyeless,
Without a guide, they cannot attain <s>bodhi</s>.
But when wisdom has been taken up among them,
Then they obtain sight—this is its designation.
Just as one skilled in painting but lacking eyes

children.text: na ca tāva puṇyu labhate akaritva cakṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Does not obtain merit until eyes are provided—
When dharmas conditioned and unconditioned, dark and bright—
Not even an atom does one apprehend when examining with wisdom—
Then one reaches the reckoning of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in the world,

children.text: ākāśa yatra na pratiṣṭhitu kiṃci tatra
children.translated_text: Like space, wherein nothing whatsoever is established.

children.text: saci manyate ahu carāmi jināna prajñāṃ
children.translated_text: If one thinks, 'I am practicing the wisdom of the <s>Jinas</s>,
I shall liberate millions of beings afflicted with many diseases'—
That <s>Bodhisattva</s> who fabricates perceptions of self and beings
Is not practicing the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has practiced the excellent <s>pāramitā</s>,

children.text: paricārikā ya na ca kāṅkṣati paṇḍitehi
children.translated_text: Who does not crave attendance from the wise—

children.text: saha śrutva tasya puna bheṣyati śāstṛsaṃjñā
children.translated_text: Upon hearing this, one will again perceive the Teacher,

children.text: so vā laghū anubudhiṣyati bodhi śāntām
children.translated_text: Or will quickly realize the peaceful <s>bodhi</s>.
Having honored millions of <s>Buddhas</s> in service,
Yet without having faith in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>—

children.text: śrutvā ca so imu kṣipiṣyati so 'lpabuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: That dull-witted one, having heard this, will reject it,
And having rejected it, will go to <s>Avīci</s> (hell), devoid of refuge.

children.text: tasmā hu śraddadhata eva jināna mātāṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, have faith in the mother of the <s>Jinas</s>,
If you wish to attain the supreme knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>.
Like a merchant who, having gone to the jewel-island,
Would cut at the root and return again empty-handed.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the seventh chapter called 'Hell.'
The purity of form should be known from the purity of its fruit,
From the purity of fruit and form, they declare the purity of omniscience.
From the purity of omniscience and fruit comes the purity of form—
Equal to the element of space, unbroken and uncut.
<s>Bodhisattvas</s> have transcended the triple world, yet
With afflictions removed, they manifest rebirth.
Free from old age, disease, and death, they display passing away—
Where the steadfast practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
The world, sunk in the mire of name, form, and existence,
Wanders in the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>, like a wind-wheel.
Knowing the world to be wandering like a deer in a snare,
The wise ones move like birds in the sky.
One who does not dwell in form, practicing with complete purity,
Nor in consciousness, perception, feeling, or volition—
Practicing thus, one abandons all attachments,
Freed from attachment, one practices the wisdom of the <s>Sugatas</s>.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the eighth chapter called 'Purification.'
Practicing thus, the wise and learned <s>Bodhisattva</s>,
With attachments cut off, moves through the world unattached,
Like the sun released from the grip of <s>Rāhu</s>, shining brilliantly,
Like fire, when supplied with fuel, burns grass, wood, and forest.
By their intrinsic nature, one sees all dharmas as utterly pure—
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees through the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na ca paśyakaṃ labhati nāpi ca sarvadharmān
children.translated_text: One finds neither a seer nor any dharmas—
This is the practice of the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the ninth chapter called 'Praise.'
<s>Śakra</s>, king of the gods, asks the <s>Jina</s>:
'How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> practicing wisdom become yoked?'

children.text: aṇumātra yo na khalu yujyati skandhadhātau
children.translated_text: 'One who is not yoked even to an atom in the aggregates and elements—'
'That very one is yoked—that is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.'
That being should be known as one who set out long ago on the great vehicle,
Who has performed service under billions of <s>Buddhas</s>,
Who, upon hearing that these dharmas are like illusions and magical creations,

children.text: na ca kāṅkṣate ayu prayujyati śikṣamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Does not doubt, but applies himself in training.
A man traveling the wilderness path with many frightened people—
When he sees the boundary of the pasture and the abundance of the forest,

children.text: āśvāsaprāpta bhavatī na ca tasya trāso
children.translated_text: He is relieved and no longer afraid:
'These are signs that villages and cities are near.'
Just so, the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>—

children.text: śṛṇu tāta yo labhati bodhi gaveṣamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Listen, friend: one who obtains it while seeking <s>bodhi</s>

children.text: āśvāsaprāpta bhavatī na ca tasya trāso
children.translated_text: Is relieved and no longer afraid,
Neither falling to the stage of an <s>Arhat</s> nor to the stage of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.
A man who goes to see the ocean waters—
If he sees trees, great forests, and mountains,

children.text: athavā na paśyati nimitta nikāṅkṣa bhoti
children.translated_text: Or does not see them—he becomes anxious about the signs:
'The great ocean is nearby, it is not far.'
Just so should one be known who has set out for excellent <s>bodhi</s>,
Hearing this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>.
Even though not predicted face to face by the guide,
Still, one will attain <s>Buddhabodhi</s> before long.
In the spring season, when grasses, leaves, and branches have fallen,
Before long, leaves, fruits, and flowers come together again.
One for whom this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has come to hand—
Before long will attain the excellent <s>bodhi</s> of the guides.

children.text: yatha istri gurviṇi ya ceṣṭati vedanābhi
children.translated_text: Just as a pregnant woman who labors with pains—
One should know that the time of her giving birth is near—
Similarly, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> hearing the wisdom of the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: rati chanda vīkṣati spṛśiṣyati bodhi śīghram
children.translated_text: Who sees delight and desire in it, will quickly attain <s>bodhi</s>.
The <s>yogin</s> (practitioner) practicing the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>

children.text: na ca rūpavṛddhi na ca paśyati pārihāṇim
children.translated_text: Sees neither increase nor decrease in form.
Neither dharma nor non-dharma—one sees this <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharma),

children.text: na ca nirvṛtiṃ spṛśati so viharāti prajñām
children.translated_text: And one does not touch <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation)—one abides in wisdom.

children.text: caramāṇu yo na iha kalpayi buddhadharmāṃ
children.translated_text: One who, while practicing, does not fabricate <s>buddhadharmās</s>,

children.text: bala ṛddhipāda na ca kalpayi bodhi śāntām
children.translated_text: Nor fabricate powers, bases of supernatural ability, nor peaceful <s>bodhi</s>—
Free from fabrication and conceptual construction, practicing with determination—
This is the practice of the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the tenth chapter called 'Qualities of Retention.'
<s>Subhūti</s> asks the <s>Buddha</s>, the moon among speakers:
'How many obstacles will there be for those delighting in these qualities?'
'Many obstacles will there be,' says the Teacher,
'I shall now proclaim just a small portion of them.'
Many and varied inspirations will arise
While one is writing this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>.
Like swift lightning, they will quickly vanish—
Without accomplishing the purpose of the world—this is <s>Māra's</s> work.
And doubt will arise in some while it is being spoken.
'My name has not been proclaimed here by the Guide,

children.text: na ca jāti bhūmi parikīrtitu nāpi gotraṃ
children.translated_text: nor has [my] birth, stage, or lineage been proclaimed —

children.text: na ca so śruṇiṣyati kṣipiṣyati mārakarma
children.translated_text: nor will he hear [this]; he will reject [it]' — this is the deed of <s>Māra</s>.
Thus, having abandoned the root, not knowing,
the deluded will seek [among] branches and leaves.
Like one who, having obtained an elephant, would search for an elephant's footprint —
so, having heard the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, one would seek [mere] discourses.
As someone who, having obtained food of a hundred flavors,
having found sixty-day-old grain on the roads, [considers it] the finest food —
so a <s>bodhisattva</s>, having obtained this <s>Pāramitā</s>,
would seek enlightenment from the stage of an <s>Arhat</s>.
They will be desirous of honor and desirous of gain,
with expectant minds, engaged in praising families.
Having abandoned the <s>Dharma</s>, they will do the work of <s>adharma</s> —
having left the path, gone on a wrong path — these are the deeds of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: ye cāpi tasmi samaye imu dharma śreṣṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: And those who at that time, regarding this supreme <s>Dharma</s>,
will produce eager faith for the sake of hearing [it] —
knowing the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher to be engaged in [proper] activity,
they will depart, led away by affection, and greatly distressed.

children.text: imi mārakarma bhaviṣyanti ya tasmi kāle
children.translated_text: These will be the deeds of <s>Māra</s> at that time,

children.text: anye ca neka vividhā bahu antarāyā
children.translated_text: and many other various and numerous obstacles,
by which many <s>bhikṣus</s> there, thrown into confusion,
will not uphold this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: ye te bhavanti ratanā ya anarghaprāptā
children.translated_text: Those who are jewels, who have attained the priceless —
they are rare, always beset by many adversaries.
Just so, the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>
is a hard-to-obtain <s>Dharma</s>-jewel, and beset by troubles.
That being of limited understanding who has set out in the new Vehicle —
who attains this hard-to-obtain <s>Dharma</s>-jewel —
<s>Māra</s> will be eager here to create obstacles,
[but] the <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions are devoted to [his] protection.
In the holy <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the eleventh chapter, named 'The Deeds of <s>Māra</s>.'

children.text: mātrāya putra bahu santi gilāni kāye
children.translated_text: A mother has many sons [who are] sick in body;
she would attend to all of them there with a sorrowful mind.
Just so, the <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions, in the world-realms,
bring to mind this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as [their] mother.
Those who are past and those who are <s>Lokanāthas</s> (Protectors of the World) in the ten directions —
from this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] they were born, and so will those of the future be.
She who shows the world, the mother who gives birth to the <s>Jinas</s>,
and she who reveals the conduct and minds of other beings.
The <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the world, the suchness of the <s>Arhats</s>,
the suchness of the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, the suchness of the <s>Jinas</s> —
it is one single suchness, free from [independent] existence, not different.
The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> was [thus] awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
Let the Knowers of the World pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> —
[this fixed order of <s>dharmas</s> remains, [whose] <s>dharmas</s> are empty;
<s>Bodhisattvas</s> awaken to that suchness —

children.text: tasmā hu buddha kṛta nāma tathāgatebhiḥ
children.translated_text: therefore the name 'Buddha' ('Awakened') was established by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.
This is the sphere and range of the Ten-Powered Guides.]
Of those who resort to the delightful grove of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> —
they rescue suffering beings from the three lower realms,

children.text: na pi sattvasaṃjña api teṣu kadāci bhoti
children.translated_text: yet the perception of 'being' never arises in them regarding those [beings].
Just as a lion, having resorted to a mountain cave,
roars fearlessly, frightening the small animals —
so the lion among men, resorting to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
roars fearlessly, frightening the various heretics.
Just as the rays of the sun, resting in the sky,
warm this earth and reveal [its] form —
so the <s>Dharma</s>-king, resting in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
dries up the river of craving and reveals the <s>Dharma</s>.
The seeing of form is the non-seeing of feeling;
the seeing of perception is the non-seeing of volition;
where there is no perception of consciousness or mind —
this seeing of <s>Dharma</s> has been taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
'I have seen space' — thus do beings declare.
Reflect on this matter: how is space seen?
In the same way, the seeing of <s>Dharma</s> has been taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s> —

children.text: na hi darśanaṃ bhaṇitu śakya nidarśanena
children.translated_text: for seeing cannot be expressed by any illustration.
In the holy <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the twelfth chapter, named 'Showing the World.'

children.text: yo eva paśyati sa paśyati sarvadharmān
children.translated_text: Whoever sees thus, sees all <s>dharmas</s>.
A king, having entrusted all activities to his ministers —
as many as are the <s>Buddha</s>-activities [arising] from the <s>dharmatā</s> of the <s>śrāvakas</s>,
the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> accomplishes all of these.

children.text: na ca rāja grāma vrajate na ca rājyarāṣṭrān
children.translated_text: A king does not go to the villages, nor to the kingdoms and countries,

children.text: sarvaṃ ca ādadati so viṣayātu āyam
children.translated_text: yet he collects all revenue from [his] domains.

children.text: na ca bodhisattva calate kvaci dharmatāyāṃ
children.translated_text: So too, a <s>bodhisattva</s> does not waver anywhere from <s>dharmatā</s>,
yet collects all the qualities in the <s>Buddha-dharma</s>.
In the holy <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the thirteenth chapter, named 'The Inconceivable.'
The <s>bodhisattva</s> whose faith in the <s>Sugata</s> is firm,
whose intention is engaged with the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
having transcended the two stages of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>,
will quickly attain the unconquerable enlightenment of the <s>Jinas</s>.
As in a seafaring ship whose body is damaged,
a hired man, not grasping grass or wood,
perishes in the midst of the water, not having reached the shore;
but one who grasps [them] goes and reaches the further shore.
Just so, one who possesses faith and has attained clarity,
yet abandons the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> alone —
then they always wander in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
in the breaking waves of birth, old age, death, and sorrow.
Those who are embraced by excellent wisdom,
skilled in the nature of existence, seeing ultimate reality —
they, whose vessel of the Vehicle is laden with the wealth of merit and knowledge,
quickly touch the supremely wondrous enlightenment of the <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: ghaṭake apakvi yatha vāri vaheya kācit
children.translated_text: Just as an unbaked pot, were it to carry water,
it should be known that it will quickly break due to [its] weakness;
[but] a well-baked pot carrying water on the road

children.text: na ca bhedanādbhayamupaiti ca svasti geham
children.translated_text: does not fear breaking and arrives safely home.
Even though a <s>bodhisattva</s> may be abundant in faith,
if devoid of wisdom, he quickly comes to ruin.
But that very faith, when embraced by wisdom,
having transcended the two [lesser] enlightenments, will attain supreme enlightenment.
Just as a ship that has not been properly prepared, in the ocean,
perishes together with the goods and the merchants;
but that very ship, when properly prepared and well-equipped,
does not break apart and reaches the shore with all its wealth intact.
Just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> cultivated by faith,
if devoid of wisdom, quickly comes to the loss of enlightenment;
but that very one, well-yoked to the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
unharmed and uninjured, touches the enlightenment of the <s>Jinas</s>.
A man who is old, suffering, one hundred and twenty years of age,

children.text: kiṃcāpi utthitu svayaṃ na prabhoti gantum
children.translated_text: though he may rise up, is unable to walk by himself;
but when supported by two men, one on each side,
there is no fear of falling, and he walks with ease.
Just so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is weak in wisdom here,
though he sets out, breaks down along the way;
but when embraced by the power of skillful means and wisdom,

children.text: na ca bhajyate spṛśati bodhi nararṣabhāṇām
children.translated_text: he does not break down and touches the enlightenment of the bulls among men.
In the holy <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the fourteenth chapter, named 'Similes.'
A <s>bodhisattva</s> who stands at the beginning stage,
who has set out with noble intention toward the enlightenment of a <s>Buddha</s> —
by them, endowed with the reverence of a good pupil toward a teacher,
a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) should always be attended upon by the wise.
For what reason? Because the attainment of virtues of the learned —
they instruct them in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Thus speaks the <s>Jina</s>, the bearer of the foremost of all virtues:
'The <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> [arise] from relying on a spiritual friend.'

children.text: dānaṃ ca śīlamapi kṣānti tathaiva vīryaṃ
children.translated_text: Giving, moral conduct, patience, likewise vigor,
meditations, and wisdom should be dedicated to enlightenment;
but one should not, having analyzed the constituents of enlightenment, cling [to them] —
those who are beginners should not be taught in this way.
Practicing thus, [they become] oceans of virtues, moons among speakers,

children.text: trāṇā bhavanti jagatī śaraṇā ca lenā
children.translated_text: protectors of the world, refuges, and shelters,
destinations, intelligences, islands, guides, desiring the welfare [of beings],
torches, meteors, excellent <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, imperturbable.
They don the armor of the difficult, the greatly renowned, girding themselves —

children.text: na ca skandhadhātu na ca āyatanaiḥ sanaddhāḥ
children.translated_text: yet not armored with aggregates, elements, or sense-bases.
Free from the perception of the three vehicles, unattached,
irreversible, unshakeable, with qualities not subject to agitation.
They, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>, are free from conceptual elaboration,
free from doubt, perplexity, and uncertainty, endowed with purpose.
Hearing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, they do not despair —
they should be known as not led by others, irreversible.
This profound <s>Dharma</s> of the Guides is difficult to see;

children.text: na ca kenacīdadhigato na ca prāpuṇanti
children.translated_text: it is not realized by anyone, nor do they attain [it].
For this purpose, having attained enlightenment, the Compassionate One [reflects:]
'With little enthusiasm — who in this mass of beings will understand this?'
And beings delight in their attachments, crave sense-objects,
established in non-grasping [yet] unawakened, being greatly blinded.
The <s>Dharma</s> that is without attachment and without grasping must be shown [to them] —
a conflict with the world has thus arisen.
In the holy <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the fifteenth chapter, named 'The Gods.'
The element of space in the eastern direction, in the southern,
likewise in the western and northern directions — infinite and boundless,
above and below, in all ten directions, as far as it extends —
there is no difference, no distinction attained.

children.text: atikrānta yā tathata yā tathatā aprāptā
children.translated_text: The suchness of the past, the suchness of what has not yet come,
the suchness of the present, the suchness of the <s>Arhats</s>,
the suchness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the suchness of the <s>Arhats</s> —
the suchness of all <s>dharmas</s> attains no distinction.
The <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to attain this —
the enlightenment of the <s>Sugatas</s>, free from the <s>dharma</s> of multiplicity —
let him be yoked to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, yoked to which
without wisdom there is no attainment for the Guides among men.
A bird whose great body [spans] a hundred <s>yojanas</s>,
with wings extending fifty [<s>yojanas</s>] on each side, weakened and powerless —
launched from the abodes of the Thirty-Three [gods] toward <s>Jambudvīpa</s>,
would cast itself down and come to ruin.
Even if one were to practice these five <s>pāramitās</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>
for many millions of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,
always cultivating vast and infinite aspirations in the world —
without skillful means and lacking in wisdom, one would fall into <s>śrāvakahood</s>.
One who wishes to go forth into <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge,
with an equal mind toward all beings, perceiving them as father and mother,
with a mind intent on benefit and a mind of loving-kindness, should strive;
with complete sincerity and gentle speech, should strive.
In the holy <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the sixteenth chapter, named 'Suchness.'
The elder <s>Subhūti</s> asks the Protector of the World:
'Describe the marks of those who are oceans of virtues, [dwelling in] non-conflict —
how the irreversible ones become beings of great power.
Explain at least a portion of the qualities of the <s>Jinas</s>.'
Free from the perception of multiplicity, speaking with fitting words,

children.text: na ca anya te śramaṇa brāhmaṇa āśrayanti
children.translated_text: they do not resort to other ascetics and brahmins.
Free from the three lower realms, they are always wise,
and they are endowed with the ten wholesome courses of action.
They teach the <s>Dharma</s> without material reward to the world,
absolutely established in the <s>Dharma</s>, always [speaking] with gentle words.
In standing, walking, lying down, and sitting — fully aware,
looking only a yoke's length ahead, they walk with unconfused thought.
Wearing clean and pure garments, purified by the threefold seclusion,

children.text: na ca lābhakāma vṛṣabhā sada dharmakāmāḥ
children.translated_text: not desiring gain, [they are] bulls, always desiring the <s>Dharma</s>.
Beyond the domain of <s>Māra</s>, not led by others,

children.text: catudhyānadhyāyi na ca niśrita tatra dhyāne
children.translated_text: practicing the four <s>dhyānas</s> yet not relying on those meditations.

children.text: na ca kīrtikāma na ca krodhaparītacittā
children.translated_text: Not desiring fame, nor with minds overcome by anger,
always unattached, having abandoned all possessions though [appearing as] householders.
They do not seek livelihood, sense-objects, or enjoyments;
they do not [use] sorcery mantras or mantras for the subjugation of women.

children.text: na ca ādiśanti puruṣaiḥ striya icchakarmāṃ
children.translated_text: They do not prescribe acts of desire between men and women;
secluded, devoted to the excellent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
free from quarrel and dispute, with firm minds of loving-kindness,
desiring omniscience, always with minds inclined toward the Teaching.
Avoiding border regions [inhabited by] barbarian peoples,
free from longing for their own territory, always like <s>Meru</s>,
they abandon [even their] life for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>, devoted to practice —
these should be known as the marks of the irreversible ones.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the seventeenth chapter, named 'The Marks and Signs of the Irreversible.'

children.text: gambhīra rupa api vedana cetanā ca
children.translated_text: Profound are form and also feeling, volition,
Consciousness and perception—by nature signless and quiescent.
Like one seeking the bottom of the ocean with a shaft of bamboo,
Having examined the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) with wisdom, one finds no ground.

children.text: yo bodhisattva imu budhyati eva dharmāṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who awakens to these very <s>dharmas</s>,
Which belong to the profound vehicle and ultimate truth and are untainted,

children.text: yasmin na skandha na pi āyatanaṃ na dhātu
children.translated_text: In which there are no <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), no <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), no <s>dhātus</s> (elements)—
How then could there be any accumulation of merit for him?
Just as a man of passionate disposition, toward a woman,
Having made an assignation but failing to obtain her, would turn back—
As many as are the mental activities of that man in a day,
That many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> comprehend.
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who for many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>

children.text: dānaṃ dadeyu vimalaṃ tatha śīla rakṣe
children.translated_text: Would give pure gifts and likewise guard morality—
Yet one who is engaged in the supreme <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)

children.text: dharmaṃ bhaṇeya kala puṇya na dānaśīle
children.translated_text: And teaches the <s>Dharma</s>—that fraction of merit is not found in generosity and morality.
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, cultivating supreme wisdom,
Having risen therefrom, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> that is untainted,
And dedicates it as a cause of awakening for the world's benefit—

children.text: nāsti triloka śubha tena samaṃ bhaveyā
children.translated_text: There is no good in the three worlds that could be equal to that.

children.text: taṃ caiva puṇya puna khyāyati riktameva
children.translated_text: Yet even that merit he again regards as empty,

children.text: tatha śūnya tuccha vaśikaṃ ca asārakaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Likewise void, hollow, deceptive, and without essence.
Thus practicing, he practices the wisdom of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones),
And while practicing, he gathers immeasurable merit.
He knows all <s>dharmas</s> as mere designations—
Taught, applied, and illuminated by the <s>Buddha</s>.
Even speaking for many <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: na ca kṣīyate na ca vivardhati dharmadhātuḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth) neither diminishes nor increases.

children.text: ye cāpi pañca imi pāramitā jinānām
children.translated_text: And also these five <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones)—
These <s>dharmas</s> too are proclaimed as mere names.
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> dedicates the merit yet does not conceive of it;
He is not diminished—he touches the supreme <s>Buddhabodhi</s> (Buddha-awakening).
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the eighteenth chapter, named 'Emptiness.'
When the wick of a lamp is burning, at the first moment of falling of the flame,

children.text: na ca dagdha varti asatā na vinā ya dagdhā
children.translated_text: The wick is not burned, nor is it burned without the non-existent flame;

children.text: na hi arci paścimanipāta sa varti dagdhā
children.translated_text: Nor is the wick burned by the last falling of the flame,

children.text: asatā pi paścima na dahyati dīpavarti
children.translated_text: Nor is the lamp-wick burned by the non-existent last flame.

children.text: prathameva citta spṛśatī na ca agrabodhim
children.translated_text: The very first mind does not touch supreme awakening,

children.text: asatā na tasya spṛśatā puna śakya bhonti
children.translated_text: Nor can the non-existent first mind be capable of touching it.
Nor does the last mind attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> (bliss),

children.text: asatā na tasya puna prāpaṇanāya śakyam
children.translated_text: Nor can the non-existent last mind be capable of attaining it.
From a seed come forth the stalk, fruit, and flower;

children.text: so vāniruddha asato na hi tasya vṛkṣo
children.translated_text: That seed has ceased—from the non-existent, there is no tree.

children.text: emeva citta prathamaṃ tu nidāna bodheḥ
children.translated_text: Just so, the first mind is the cause of awakening;

children.text: so vā niruddha asato na hi tasya bodhiḥ
children.translated_text: But that mind has ceased—from the non-existent, there is no awakening.
Dependent on a seed, there comes to be the fruit of barley, rice, and such;

children.text: tattatphalaṃ na ca tadasti na cāpi nāsti
children.translated_text: Each respective fruit—it neither exists nor does it not exist.
From origination arises this awakening of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones),
Devoid of inherent nature of being—here it is like an illusion.
A water pot is filled drop by drop, little by little;
From the first drop, gradually, to the last.
Just so, the first mind is the cause of supreme awakening;
Gradually, filled with pure qualities, they become <s>Buddhas</s>.
Practicing the <s>dharmas</s> of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness,

children.text: na ca nirvṛtiṃ spṛśati no ca nimittacārī
children.translated_text: He neither touches <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) nor engages in signs.
Just as a skillful boatman goes from this shore to the far shore,
Standing on neither bank, he does not remain in the ocean.

children.text: evaṃ carantu na ca manyati bodhisattvo
children.translated_text: Thus practicing, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not conceive:
'I have been predicted by the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten-Powered One); I shall touch awakening.'

children.text: na ca trāsu bodhi bhavate na ihāsti kiṃcid
children.translated_text: Nor is there fear regarding awakening, nor is there anything here;
Thus practicing, he practices the wisdom of the <s>Sugatas</s>.
Seeing the world as a wilderness-path, afflicted by famine, beset with disease,
And seeing there is no other fear, he girds himself further.
Always engaged, knowing the furthest limit of existence,
He does not take up even the slightest weariness of mind.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the nineteenth chapter, named 'The Sister of the Goddess <s>Gaṅgā</s>.'
Again, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practicing the wisdom of the <s>Jinas</s>,
Without clinging, knows these <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as primordially empty.
Even without formal concentration, he beholds with compassion the realm of beings;
In the meantime, he does not decline from the <s>Buddhadharmas</s>.
Just as a skillful man, endowed with all qualities,
Strong, indomitable, accomplished in practice, versed in the arts,
Having mastered archery and weapons, skilled in many crafts,
Supreme in knowledge of magic arts, desiring the world's welfare—
Taking up his mother and father, together with his sons and wife,
Setting out on a wilderness-path, with many friends,
He, having conjured many brave and heroic men,
Would go safely and return again to his home.
Just so, at the time when the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>
Extends great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) to the entire realm of beings,

children.text: caturo sa māra atikramya dvaye ca bhūmim
children.translated_text: Having transcended the four <s>Māras</s> and the two levels,

children.text: asmin samādhi sthitu no ca spṛśāti bodhim
children.translated_text: He abides in this <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) yet does not touch awakening.
Depending on space are wind and the aggregate of water;

children.text: ta hi niśritā iha mahāpṛthivī jagacca
children.translated_text: Depending on them are the great earth and the world.
The very cause of beings' <s>karma</s> and experience—
Standing in space—contemplate this matter: where is it?
Just so, established in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), this being
Displays in the world various and manifold activities.
Through the very power of knowledge and aspiration for beings,

children.text: na ca nirvṛtiṃ spṛśati śūnyata nāsti sthānam
children.translated_text: He does not touch cessation—in emptiness there is no abiding place.
At which time the wise, learned <s>Bodhisattva</s>

children.text: caratī imāṃ pravara śūnya samādhi śāntām
children.translated_text: Practices this excellent, empty, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>,
In the meantime, he should not cultivate signs;
Nor, abiding in the signless, should he be one who practices mere quiescence.
A bird going through the sky leaves no footprints;

children.text: no cāpi tatra sthitu no ca patāti bhūmau
children.translated_text: Neither does it remain there, nor does it fall to the ground.
Likewise, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practicing the gates of liberation—

children.text: na ca nirvṛtiṃ spṛśati no ca nimittacārī
children.translated_text: He neither touches cessation nor engages in signs.
Just as a man trained in archery, having shot an arrow upward,
Then shooting another arrow, one after another,

children.text: patanāya tasya purimasya na deya bhūmim
children.translated_text: Does not give ground for the falling of the first—
The arrow would fall only when the man so desires.
Just so, one practicing the supreme <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom),
Reflecting on wisdom, means, power, and supernatural ability—
He does not attain that supreme emptiness
So long as his roots of merit are not yet fulfilled.
Just as a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) endowed with the supreme power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural ability),
Stationed in the sky, performs the <s>yamaka prātihārya</s> (twin miracle),
Displaying going, walking, lying down, and sitting—

children.text: na nivartate na pi ca khidyati yāva tatra
children.translated_text: He neither turns back nor grows weary as long as he remains there.
Just so, the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in emptiness,
Having reached the far shore of knowledge and supernatural ability, wandering without abode,
Displays in the world infinite and various activities;

children.text: na ca bhajyatī na pi ca khidyati kalpakoṭī
children.translated_text: He neither is broken nor grows weary for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>.
Just as some men, standing at a great precipice,
Taking two umbrellas in both hands, would jump off,
Releasing themselves into the air at the great precipice—

children.text: no ca prapāta patiyāti na yāva tatra
children.translated_text: They do not fall down the precipice so long as the umbrellas hold.
Just so, the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>, abiding in compassion,
Grasping the twin umbrellas of wisdom and skillful means,
Examines <s>dharmas</s> through emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;

children.text: na ca nirvṛtiṃ spṛśati paśyati dharmacārī
children.translated_text: He does not touch cessation, yet sees—he is a practitioner of the <s>Dharma</s>.
Just as one seeking jewels, having traveled to the jewel island,
Having obtained jewels, would return again to his home—
Although the caravan-leader lives happily there,

children.text: api duḥkhito manasi bhoti sa jātisaṃgho
children.translated_text: Yet in his mind he is grieved by the association with further births.
Just so, having traveled to the jewel island of emptiness,
Having obtained the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), powers, and faculties, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>—
Although he might touch cessation with delight,
Yet all beings' suffering remains in his mind.

children.text: abhyantare ya nagare nigame ca grāme
children.translated_text: In the interior, in cities, market-towns, and villages,
Just as a merchant goes about for the sake of profit, knowing the routes—

children.text: no cāpi tatra sthihatī na ca ratnadvīpe
children.translated_text: He neither remains there, nor on the jewel island,

children.text: na ca geha mārgi kuśalo puna bhoti vijño
children.translated_text: Nor does the skillful, discerning one again become a homebody on the road.
Likewise, in the knowledge of the liberation of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,
The wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> is skillful everywhere;

children.text: no cāpi tatra sthihate na ca buddhajñāne
children.translated_text: He neither remains there, nor in <s>Buddhajñāna</s> (Buddha-knowledge),

children.text: na ca saṃskṛte bhavati mārgavidū vidhijño
children.translated_text: Nor does the knower of the path, versed in the method, remain in the conditioned.
When, having extended <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) to the world,
He practices the <s>samādhi</s> of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—
It is impossible that he should attain cessation,
Or that he could be designated as conditioned.

children.text: yatha nirmito puruṣa no va adṛśyakāyo
children.translated_text: Just as a conjured man—his body is not invisible,

children.text: nāmena vā puna sa prajñapanāya śakyaḥ
children.translated_text: Yet he cannot be designated by name.
Likewise, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practicing the gates of liberation—

children.text: nāmena vā puna sa prajñapanāya śakyaḥ
children.translated_text: He too cannot be designated by name.
If, when questioned, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practicing the faculties
Does not illuminate the profound <s>dharmas</s>,
The emptiness, signlessness, and <s>dharmas</s> of irreversible awakening—

children.text: na ca śocatī na ca sa vyākṛtu veditavyo
children.translated_text: And does not grieve—he should not be known as one who has been predicted.
Even the <s>Arhat</s>-level and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-level,
And the three realms—he does not touch even in a dream.
He sees the <s>Buddhas</s> and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings—
He should be known as irreversible—he has been predicted.
Seeing in a dream beings who have reached the three lower realms,
He makes a vow: 'In that instant, may I dry up the lower realms.'
Through the power of truth (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>), he also pacifies a mass of fire—
He should be known as irreversible—he has been predicted.
Demonic possessions and various diseases in the mortal world—
Through the power of truth, the compassionate one pacifies them.

children.text: na ca tena manyanupapadyati nāpi mānam
children.translated_text: Neither pride nor conceit arises from that—
He should be known as irreversible—he has been predicted.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the twentieth chapter, named 'Examination of Skill in Means.'
Or if pride arises in him thinking 'I have been predicted,'
'Various powers of truth are flourishing in me'—
If the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conceives pride regarding one predicted by another,
He should be known as one established in conceit, of small wisdom.
Again, <s>Māra</s>, having approached through the basis of name,
Will speak thus: 'This is your name;
Your lineage traces through your mother and father;

children.text: buddho yadā bhavi idaṃ tava nāmadheyam
children.translated_text: When you become a <s>Buddha</s>, this will be your name.'
'Such ascetic practices you will have; you will be an accomplished practitioner;

children.text: pūrvaṃ pi tubhya imi āsi guṇovarūpā
children.translated_text: Even formerly, these were your distinguished qualities.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, having heard this, conceives pride—
He should be known as overwhelmed by <s>Māra</s>, of small wisdom.
Secluded from villages and cities, dwelling in mountain caves,
In the forest, secluded, frequenting woodland retreats—
If the <s>Bodhisattva</s> exalts himself and disparages others,
He should be known as overwhelmed by <s>Māra</s>, of small wisdom.

children.text: grāme ca rāṣṭri nigame viharanti nityaṃ
children.translated_text: Those who constantly dwell in villages, kingdoms, and market-towns,
Who generate the conditions for solitude and aspiration there—
Except when engaged in the ripening of beings for awakening—
This is the seclusion taught for the sons of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones).
One who for five hundred <s>yojanas</s>, in mountain caves
Infested with wild beasts, would dwell for many <s>koṭis</s> of years—

children.text: no cā viveku imu jānati bodhisattvo
children.translated_text: If the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not know this true seclusion,
He dwells in confusion, seized by presumption.
He looks down upon <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are diligently engaged, walking about for exercise,
Who have attained the powers, <s>dhyānas</s>, faculties, liberations, and <s>samādhis</s>—
Thinking 'These are not practitioners of forest seclusion'—

children.text: na vivekagocaru ayaṃ hi jinena ukto
children.translated_text: But he himself is not in the domain of seclusion as taught by the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One).
Whether one dwells at the edge of a village or in the forest,
Free from the thought of the two vehicles, determined for supreme awakening—
This is the seclusion of those who have set out for the welfare of the world.
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who measures himself against others wastes himself.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the twenty-first chapter, named 'The Deeds of <s>Māra</s>.'
Therefore, the wise one, having struck down conceit,
With a weighty resolve, seeking supreme awakening—
Just as a sick person seeks a physician for the treatment of his own disease,
So should a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) be served by the diligent one.
<s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set out for supreme awakening—
These spiritual friends have taught the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).
They are the instructors; this is the stage of practice.
Through these two causes, one awakens to <s>Buddhabodhi</s> (Buddha-awakening).
The <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) past and future, and those established in the ten directions—
In all paths, this <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) is unequaled,
a radiance, a torch for those who have set out toward supreme awakening,
a light, a teacher — these <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) have been taught.
Just as <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) is characterized by emptiness,
so one who knows all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) as having that same characteristic,
understanding <s>dharmas</s> as empty and without characteristics,
practicing thus, one practices the wisdom of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones).
Beings who desire nourishment, engaging in conceptual proliferation,
with minds attached to <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), always recollect:

children.text: ahu mahya dharma ubhi eti abhūta śūnyā
children.translated_text: 'These are my <s>dharmas</s> on both sides' — yet they are unreal and empty.
Like a knot in space, they bind themselves, these fools.
Just as one who is fearful approaches what is perceived as poison,

children.text: no cāsya koṣṭhagatu so viṣu pātyate ca
children.translated_text: and though the poison has not entered his stomach, he falls as if poisoned,
so too the fool who grasps, thinking 'this is mine,'

children.text: ahasaṃjñi jāyi mriyate ca sadā abhūto
children.translated_text: with the perception of self, is born and dies, always in unreality.
As is the grasping, so is the defilement revealed;
purification is declared as the non-apprehension of 'I' and 'mine.'

children.text: na hi atra kaści yo kliśyati śudhyate vā
children.translated_text: For there is no one here who is defiled or purified;
through the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> awakens.
However many beings there are in all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>,
if they all, having generated the mind of supreme awakening,
gave gifts for many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of years,
and dedicated all that to the world's benefit for awakening —
yet one who is devoted to the supreme <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
even for just a single day, following it,

children.text: kalapuṇya so na bhavatī iha dānaskandho
children.translated_text: that heap of merit from giving does not equal even a fraction of this;
therefore, one should always diligently pursue wisdom.
The practitioner who walks in the supreme <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>

children.text: mahatīṃ janeti karuṇāṃ na ca sattvasaṃjñā
children.translated_text: generates great compassion, yet without the perception of beings;
then they become worthy of offerings from all the world,
and constantly, without waste, they enjoy the alms of the realm.
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who wishes to liberate beings
from long cycles among <s>devas</s> (gods), humans, and the three lower realms,
shows the broad path, the crossing, to the realm of beings;

children.text: prajñāya pāramita yukta divā ca rātrau
children.translated_text: united with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> day and night.
A person who previously had never obtained a precious jewel,

children.text: aparasmi kāli puna labdhva bhaveya tuṣṭo
children.translated_text: having obtained one at another time, would be delighted;

children.text: sa ha labdhva nāśayi puno 'pi pramādabhūto
children.translated_text: but if, having obtained it, he loses it again through carelessness,
having lost it, he would always be sorrowful, longing for the jewel.
Just so, one who has set out for supreme awakening — it is like a jewel;
the practice of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not be abandoned.
Like one who, having obtained a jewel, holds it with undivided mind,
one quickly awakens and attains peace.
In the blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the chapter on spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitraparivarta</s>), the twenty-second.
When the sun rises, its garland of rays goes forth,
dispelling all darkness that obscures with gloom;
it outshines all the glow of fireflies and luminous creatures,
and all the hosts of stars, and even the moon's radiance.
Just so, the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> who practices the supreme <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>
dispels the thicket of wrong views;
one outshines all the world, and the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary realizers) too,
the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is vast, whose conduct is emptiness and signlessness.
Just as a prince who bestows wealth, desiring the welfare of all,
becomes the foremost among all in approachability —
he already now liberates beings;
how much more when he is established in kingship, wearing the royal diadem!
Just so, the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose conduct is wisdom,
the bestower of the deathless, dear to <s>devas</s> and humans —
this one seeks the goal, devoted to the happiness of beings;
how much more when established as the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of the Dharma)!
In the blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the chapter on <s>Śakra</s>, the twenty-third.
At that time, <s>Māra</s> too becomes pierced with thorns of grief,
sorrowful, suffering, his mind boundless in anguish, his strength diminished;
he hurls blazing firebrands in the directions to create a terrifying sight,
[wondering,] 'How can this one of feeble mind become a <s>Bodhisattva</s>?'
When those wise ones are endowed with pure intention,
seeing the meaning of the supreme <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> day and night,
then their body and mind become like the wings of a bird —
where will the kinsman of darkness (<s>Kṛṣṇabandhu</s>) find an opening?
When <s>Bodhisattvas</s> engage in quarrels and disputes,
becoming mutually hostile with angry minds,

children.text: tada māra tuṣṭu bhavatī paramaṃ udagro
children.translated_text: then <s>Māra</s> becomes supremely delighted and elated:

children.text: ubhi eti dūra bhaviṣyanti jināna jñāne
children.translated_text: 'Both will be far from the knowledge of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones).'
'Both will be far away, like <s>piśācas</s> (malevolent spirits);
both will bring ruin upon their own vows.
For those who are corrupt and lacking in patience, where is awakening?'
Then <s>Māra</s> <s>Namuci</s> together with his faction is delighted.
If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has received a prediction, toward another who has received a prediction,
corrupts their mind and initiates a dispute,
for as many mind-moments as are accompanied by the fault of hostility,
for that many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) one must again don the armor of practice.
But if there arises the thought, 'This is unseemly,'
[knowing that] the <s>Buddhas</s> touch awakening through the perfection of patience,
one demonstrates restraint again in the future,

children.text: apayāti vā sa iha śikṣati buddhadharme
children.translated_text: or, approaching the other, trains here in the <s>Buddhadharma</s>.
In the blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the chapter on pride (<s>abhimānaparivarta</s>), the twenty-fourth.

children.text: yo śikṣamāṇu na upaiti kahiṃci śikṣāṃ
children.translated_text: One who, while training, does not approach any training,

children.text: na ca śikṣakaṃ labhati nāpi ca śikṣadharmān
children.translated_text: and finds neither a trainer nor the <s>dharmas</s> of training,
not conceptualizing either training or non-training —

children.text: yo śikṣate sa iha śikṣati buddhadharme
children.translated_text: one who trains thus, trains here in the <s>Buddhadharma</s>.

children.text: yo bodhisattva imu jānati eva śikṣāṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who knows this training in this way

children.text: na sa jātu śikṣavikalo bhavate duśīlo
children.translated_text: never becomes deficient in training or of poor conduct;
having pleased the <s>Buddhas</s>, one trains here in the <s>Buddhadharma</s>,
skillful in training and beyond-training, through non-apprehension.
In the very training of the wise, the light-makers,
not even a single unwholesome thought arises;
just as when the sun moves across the sky in the atmosphere,
wherever its rays reach, darkness does not remain before it.
In the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> training regarding the conditioned,
all the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are included.

children.text: satkāyadṛṣṭi yatha ṣaṣṭi duve ca dṛṣṭī
children.translated_text: Just as in the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the sixty-two views
are included, so too are these <s>pāramitās</s>.
Just as when the life faculty ceases, whatever other
faculties there are, extensive as they may be, all cease,
so too in the wisdom-practice of the wise, supreme ones,
all the <s>pāramitās</s> are said to be included.
Whatever qualities of <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary realizers) there are,
the wise <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who train possess them all;

children.text: no cāpi tatra sthihatāna spṛheti teṣām
children.translated_text: yet they do not desire to remain in those attainments,
thinking, 'This is to be trained in,' they train for this purpose.
In the blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the chapter on training (<s>śikṣāparivarta</s>), the twenty-fifth.
When one rejoices with pure intention
in the generation of mind of the irreversible one who has set out for supreme awakening,
even if one were to weigh the <s>Meru</s> mountains of the three-thousandfold world system, that would be measurable,
but not this rejoicing in that wholesome merit.
However many beings there are who desire wholesome aims and seek liberation,
all their heaps of merit from rejoicing —
seeking the welfare of beings, having attained the infinite qualities of the <s>Jinas</s>,
they will give the <s>Dharma</s> to the world for the complete cessation of suffering.
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is free from conceptualization regarding all <s>dharmas</s>,
who fully knows them as empty, signless, and free from elaboration,

children.text: na ca prajña bodhi parieṣati āśayena
children.translated_text: yet does not seek wisdom or awakening with grasping intention —
that practitioner is yoked to the supreme <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
There could be an obstruction of the space-element of the sky,

children.text: na hi tena tasya kutu kenacideṣa prāptā
children.translated_text: but by no one anywhere has this wisdom been attained as an object;
just so, the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose conduct is wisdom
is like open space, of peaceful conduct.
Just as for a magician, there never arises

children.text: te śiṣya māṃ janata so ca karoti kāryam
children.translated_text: the thought 'May these pupils know me,' yet he performs his work,
and they see him displaying various acts —

children.text: na ca tasya kāyu na pi citta na nāmadheyam
children.translated_text: yet he has no body, no mind, no name.
Just so, in the practice of wisdom there never arises
the thought 'Having awakened to awakening, having liberated the world' —
yet one displays various births and engagement in actions,
like an illusion, without conceptual conduct.

children.text: yatha buddha nirmita karoti ca buddhakāryaṃ
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>Buddha</s>'s emanation performs the <s>Buddha</s>'s work,

children.text: na ca tasyupadyati mado karamāṇu kiṃcit
children.translated_text: yet no pride arises in it while doing anything,
just so, the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose conduct is wisdom
displays all actions as equal to an emanation, an illusion.
A wooden automaton made by a skilled carpenter,

children.text: puruṣe stritulya sa karoti ha sarvakāryam
children.translated_text: resembling a man or woman, performs all tasks;
just so, the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose conduct is wisdom
performs all actions through knowledge, free from conceptualization.
In the blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the chapter on the illusion-like (<s>māyopamaparivarta</s>), the twenty-sixth.
When one practices thus, the vast assemblies of <s>devas</s> and <s>Nāgas</s>,
with palms joined in reverence, bowing down, pay homage;
and <s>Buddhas</s> throughout the world-systems in the ten directions
proclaim garlands of praise for their qualities.
In as many fields as there are grains of sand in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River,

children.text: sattvā ta sarvi parikalpa bhaveyu mārāḥ
children.translated_text: if all the beings therein were to become <s>Māras</s>,
and each one further emanated that many <s>Māras</s>,

children.text: sarve na śakya karaṇe vidu antarāyam
children.translated_text: none of them would be able to create an obstacle for the wise one.
For four reasons the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> is powerful,
unassailable, unshakeable by the four <s>Māras</s>:
one abides in emptiness yet does not abandon beings,
one speaks truthfully, and one's state is pervaded by compassion for beings.
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has faith in this
<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the mother of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Thus-Gone Ones), when it is taught,
and who engages in its practice with pure intention —
that one should be known as having set out for omniscience.
