One does not approach a standing-place in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) or <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),
yet one is established in the non-standing, light as the sky,
like a <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder) who, intending to reach the forest, hangs in the air,
a bird at a dead tree, sustained by the power of <s>mantras</s>.
Thus practicing, the wise, learned <s>Bodhisattva</s>

children.text: na ca budhyakaṃ labhati nāpi ca buddhadharmān
children.translated_text: finds neither one who awakens nor the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>,

children.text: na ca deśikaṃ na pi ca paśyaka dharmatāyāṃ
children.translated_text: neither a teacher nor an observer in the nature of reality;
this is the abode of those who seek peace, delighting in qualities.
However many are the abodes of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,
peaceful, connected with the tranquility of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and happiness,
setting aside the liberation of <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Tathāgatas</s>,
this abode is supreme and unsurpassed among all.

children.text: ākāśi pakṣi viharāti na co patāti
children.translated_text: A bird abides in the sky and does not fall;

children.text: dakamadhyi matsya viharāti na co marāti
children.translated_text: a fish abides in the water and does not die;
just so, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has gone beyond in the power of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation)
abides in emptiness yet does not attain <s>nirvṛti</s> (final cessation).
One who wishes to reach the foremost of all beings' qualities,
who would touch the supreme, most wondrous <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge,
who would give the supreme, excellent, highest gift of <s>Dharma</s> —
let them cultivate this supreme abode of those who work for benefit.
In the blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the chapter on the essence (<s>sāraparivarta</s>), the twenty-seventh.
However many trainings have been illuminated by the Guide,

children.text: sarveṣa śikṣa ayu agru niruttarā ca
children.translated_text: this training is supreme and unsurpassed among all;
one who, knowing all trainings, wishes to go beyond —
this one trains in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the training of the <s>Buddhas</s>.
This is the supreme treasure, the highest storehouse of <s>Dharma</s>,
generating the lineage of <s>Buddhas</s>, a treasury of happiness and bliss;
the <s>Lokanāthas</s> (World-Protectors) of past and future in the ten directions

children.text: itu te prasūta na ca kṣīyati dharmadhātuḥ
children.translated_text: are born from this, yet the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is not diminished.
However many trees, fruit-bearing, flowering, and plants there are,
all have arisen emerging from the earth,

children.text: na ca medinī kṣayamupaiti na cāpi vṛddhiṃ
children.translated_text: yet the earth undergoes neither decrease nor increase,

children.text: na ca khidyatī na parihāyati nirvikalpā
children.translated_text: it is not wearied, nor does it decline — it is free from conceptualization.
However many <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> there are,
along with <s>devas</s> and all the world's <s>dharmas</s> of happiness and bliss,
all are born from the supreme <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>;

children.text: na ca kṣīyate na ca vivardhati jātu prajñā
children.translated_text: yet wisdom never diminishes nor increases.
However many beings of inferior, middling, or superior faculties there are in the world,
all are declared by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) to originate from ignorance;
the mechanism of suffering operates through the conjunction of conditions,

children.text: na ca yantra kṣīyati avidya na cāpi vṛddhiḥ
children.translated_text: yet the mechanism does not diminish — ignorance neither decreases nor increases.
However many knowledges, gateways of method, and roots of skillful means there are,
all are born from the supreme <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>;
the mechanism of knowledge operates through the conjunction of conditions,

children.text: na ca prajñapāramita vardhati hīyate vā
children.translated_text: yet the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> neither increases nor diminishes.
One who understands <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) as non-arising,
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who understands this wisdom as inexhaustible
Is like the sun with rays released from a covering of clouds—
Having dispelled the veil of ignorance, he becomes the Self-Arisen One.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the twenty-eighth chapter, named The Scattered Flowers Chapter (<s>Avakīrṇakusumaparivarta</s>).
The great powerful ones abide in the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions),

children.text: na ca ālayo na pi ca niśrayu kurvayāti
children.translated_text: Yet they do not create attachment or dependence [on them].

children.text: api kho punāśrayu ime catudhyāna sāṅgā
children.translated_text: Moreover, will these four <s>dhyānas</s> with their branches
Serve for the attainment of the supreme, noble <s>bodhi</s>?
Abiding here in <s>dhyāna</s>, one becomes an obtainer of excellent wisdom;
The four supreme <s>samādhis</s> of the formless and form [realms]—
These <s>dhyānas</s> are helpful for supreme, foremost awakening,
But the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trains so that the outflows do not diminish [his resolve].
Wondrous and marvelous is this of those who accumulate virtues:
They abide in <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>, yet there is no sign [of attachment].
For those established there, when their bodily existence breaks up,
They are reborn in the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (Desire Realm) according to their intention.
Just as humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who have never before obtained
The supreme divine cities in the heavens might reach them,
And having seen those pleasures received there,

children.text: punarāgameya na ca niśrayu tatra kuryāt
children.translated_text: Might return again without creating dependence there—
In the same way, those virtue-bearing, excellent <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,
Having abided in <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>, diligent in yoga,
Again stand in the Desire Realm, unstained—
Like a lotus in water, not clinging to childish ways.
Otherwise, [engaged in] maturing beings and purifying fields,
For the purpose of fulfilling these <s>pāramitās</s>, the great soul
Does not aspire to rebirth in the Formless Realm,
Where there is loss of the <s>bodhi</s>-qualities and <s>pāramitās</s>.
Just as a certain person, having found a treasure-trove of gems,

children.text: labdhvā tu tatra spṛhabuddhi na saṃjaneyyā
children.translated_text: Would not generate a greedy mind toward it,

children.text: ekāki so puna gṛhītva parasmi kāle
children.translated_text: But alone, having taken it at another time,

children.text: gṛhṇitva geha praviśitva na bhoti lubdho
children.translated_text: Entering his house, he is not greedy—
In the same way, having obtained the four peaceful <s>dhyāna samādhis</s>,
Productive of joy and bliss, the wise <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,
Abandoning the gain of the bliss, joy, and <s>samādhi</s> of <s>dhyāna</s>,
Enter the Desire Realm again, out of compassion for the world.
If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> abides in <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhyāna</s>
And generates a greedy mind toward the fruits of the solitary [paths],
[Or] becomes distracted with an agitated, scattered mind—
[He is] one whose wisdom-qualities have declined, like a captain with a broken ship.
Though he may be endowed with form, sound, likewise scent,

children.text: rasa sparśa kāmaguṇa pañcabhi yukta bhogī
children.translated_text: Taste, touch—enjoying the five sense-pleasures—
The irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s>, free from the fruits of the solitary [paths],
Is to be known as a hero, constantly concentrated.
Purified through the cause of other beings and persons,
They wander about, endowed with the <s>pāramitā</s> of vigor and power.
Just as a slave-woman [serves] the master, whether willingly or unwillingly—
So the steadfast ones submit to the service of all beings.

children.text: na ca svāmikasya prativākyu dadāti dāsī
children.translated_text: The slave-woman does not talk back to her master,

children.text: ākruṣṭa cāpi athavā sada tāḍitā vā
children.translated_text: Even when abused or constantly beaten—
Thoroughly terrified in mind, overpowered by fear,
[Thinking:] He will surely kill me for some reason.
In the same way, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set forth toward supreme <s>bodhi</s>
Should stand toward all the world as a servant.
Upon attaining <s>bodhi</s> and the fulfillment of qualities,
Fire born from grass and wood burns that very [fuel].
Having given up self for the welfare of other beings [as if for] the <s>Sugatas</s>,
Diligent day and night, with a mind free from expectations,
Caring [for beings] as a mother cares for her only child—
In [this] aspiration, unwearied, he attends [to them].
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the twenty-ninth chapter, named The Conformity Chapter (<s>Anugamaparivarta</s>).
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who intends long wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>,
Diligent in yoga for the welfare of beings and purification of fields,
Does not take up even the slightest thought of weariness—
He is endowed with the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Energy) and is untiring.
If a wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to count <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,
[Thinking:] I shall accomplish <s>bodhi</s> through long suffering,
[Thinking:] There will be long suffering while practicing the <s>Dharma</s>—
Then he is deficient in the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s>, of lazy form.
From the first arising of the mind toward supreme <s>bodhi</s>,
Until he attains the supreme, auspicious [<s>nirvāṇa</s>],
He should establish himself with single-minded [focus] day and night—
Such a one, the wise and learned, is to be known as possessing initiating vigor.
If someone were to say: Having split Mount <s>Sumeru</s>,
Afterward you will attain supreme <s>bodhi</s>—
If he generates a thought of weariness and a thought of measuring [the difficulty],
Then that <s>Bodhisattva</s> has fallen into laziness.
But if the thought arises in him: How small a matter!
In an instant it reduces <s>Sumeru</s> to ashes and dissolution—
That wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> possesses initiating vigor
And will before long attain the supreme <s>bodhi</s> of the Guides.
If he were to exert himself by body, mind, and speech,
[Thinking:] Having matured the world, I shall accomplish its welfare—
[But] stands with the perception of self, he has fallen into laziness,
Far from the cultivation of non-self, as the sky from the earth.

children.text: yasminna kāyu na pi citta na sattvasaṃjñā
children.translated_text: Where there is no body, no mind, no perception of beings,
[But] standing in the reversal of perception, practicing the non-dual <s>dharma</s>—
This is called the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> by the Beneficent One,
For one aspiring to the supreme, imperishable, auspicious <s>bodhi</s>.
Having heard harsh, ill-spoken words from others,
The wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> is well-pleased and happy.

children.text: ko bhāṣate ka śṛṇute kutu kasya kena
children.translated_text: Who speaks? Who hears? From where? To whom? By what?
That wise one is established in the practice of the noble <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience).
That <s>Bodhisattva</s> who endures, endowed with virtuous qualities—
[Even] one who were to give the <s>trisāhasra</s> (three-thousandfold world) filled with jewels
To <s>Buddhas</s>, world-knowers, <s>Arhats</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>—

children.text: kalapuṇya so na bhavate iha dānaskandhe
children.translated_text: [That] would not be a fraction of the merit in this mass of giving.
For one established in patience, his bodily existence is purified,
The splendor of the thirty-two marks is endless and boundless.
[He] causes beings to hear the noble <s>dharma</s> of emptiness,
He becomes dear to all the world, the wise one who endures.
If some being were to take a packet of sandalwood paste
And reverently anoint the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with great love,
While another were to cast fire upon his head—
Toward both, an equal mind should be taken up by him.
Having thus endured, the wise, learned <s>Bodhisattva</s>
Turns that mind-generation toward supreme <s>bodhi</s>.
As many [acts of] patience as there are for the solitary ones and beings—
The hero who endures surpasses all the world.
While enduring, this mind should be taken up:
In the hells, in the animal realm, in <s>Yamaloka</s>—many are the sufferings
Experienced for the sake of sense-pleasures, against one's will.

children.text: kasmā hu adya na kṣameya nidāna bodhau
children.translated_text: Why then should I not endure now, for the sake of <s>bodhi</s>?
Whippings, beatings with sticks, slaying with weapons, bondage, and blows,
Cutting off of head, ears, feet, hands, and nose—
As many sufferings as there are in the world—I shall bear them all!
That <s>Bodhisattva</s> stands in the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience).
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the thirtieth chapter, named The Chapter of <s>Sadāprarudita</s> (Ever-Weeping) (<s>Sadāpraruditaparivarta</s>).
Through morality (<s>śīla</s>), they rise up, aspiring to <s>samādhi</s>,
Established in the range of the Ten-Powered Ones, with morality unbroken.
As many moral restraints as they follow,
They turn all toward <s>bodhi</s> for the welfare of all beings.
If one generates aspiration for the awakening of the solitary [<s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>],
One becomes
of bad morality, a transgressor in the view of the wise.
But if one turns [one's merit] toward the supreme, auspicious <s>bodhi</s>,
One stands in the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Morality), even while endowed with sense-pleasures.
The <s>Dharma</s> that leads to the <s>bodhi</s>-qualities of the heroes—
That is the meaning of morality for those endowed with virtuous qualities.
The <s>Dharma</s> that leads to the loss of <s>bodhi</s>-qualities for the beneficent—
That is declared by the Guide to be bad morality.
If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> enjoys the five sense-pleasures
[While maintaining] refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the Noble <s>Saṃgha</s>,
[Thinking:] I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, with omniscience in mind—
He is to be known as the wise one established in the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>.
If, practicing through ten <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> on the ten wholesome paths,
One generates aspiration for the <s>Arhat</s>'s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>'s [fruition]—
Then one becomes of broken morality, of perforated morality,
Defeated (<s>pārājika</s>)—graver is this mind-generation.
Guarding morality, turning [it] toward supreme <s>bodhi</s>,

children.text: na ca tena manyati na ātmana karṣayethā
children.translated_text: Yet not conceiving thereby, nor tormenting himself—
With self-perception abandoned and being-perception cast aside,
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is said to stand in the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>.
If a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, practicing on the <s>Jinas</s>' path,
Considers these moral ones and those of bad morality as beings [to be distinguished]—
Given over to the perception of multiplicity, he is supremely immoral,

children.text: api chidraśīlu na tu so pariśuddhaśīlo
children.translated_text: Of perforated morality too—he is not of pure morality.

children.text: yasyo na asti ahasaṃjña na sattvasaṃjñā
children.translated_text: One who has no perception of self, nor perception of beings,
Being detached from perception—where would there be non-restraint for him?
For one in whom there is no conceiving of restraint or non-restraint—
This is the moral restraint declared by the Guide.
One who is thus endowed with morality, free from conceptual elaboration,
Becomes indifferent toward all that is dear and not dear.
Giving up head, hands, and feet, with undaunted mind,
He becomes an all-relinquisher, constantly alert.
Having known the nature of <s>dharmas</s> as selfless and under control,
Giving up his own flesh with undaunted mind—
How much more so external possessions! He would not fail to give them.
It is impossible that he would be miserly.
From self-perception arises possessiveness and attachment;
Where would there be a thought of giving among the deluded?
Through miserliness one becomes a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) and is reborn [there],
Or, if human, one becomes poor in form.
Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having known these poor beings,
Becomes devoted to giving, constantly practicing open-handed generosity.
Having given the four continents, adorned, as if a ball—

children.text: dattvā udagra bhavate na hi dvīpalabdho
children.translated_text: He is elated, for he does not apprehend the continents.
Having given gifts, the wise, learned <s>Bodhisattva</s>,
Having gathered together all beings in the three realms of existence,
For all of them this gift has been given—
And he turns that toward supreme <s>bodhi</s> for the world's welfare.

children.text: na ca vastuniśrayu karoti daditva dānaṃ
children.translated_text: He does not create dependence on the object after giving the gift;

children.text: vidu pāku naiva pratikāṅkṣati so kadācit
children.translated_text: The wise one never expects a ripening [reward].
Having thus relinquished, the wise one becomes an all-relinquisher;
Having relinquished little, he obtains much, immeasurable.
As many beings as there are in the three realms of existence without remainder—
If all of them were to give gifts for endless <s>kalpas</s>,
Looking to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the wise, <s>Arhats</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,
And conceive of the qualities of hearers in those stations—
Yet a wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>, skilled in means,
Having rejoiced in their basis of meritorious action,
Would turn [that merit] toward the welfare of beings and supreme <s>bodhi</s>—
Endowed with dedication, he surpasses all the world.

children.text: kācasya vā maṇina rāśi siyā mahanto
children.translated_text: There might be a great heap of glass and gems—
[But] a single <s>vaiḍūrya</s> jewel surpasses them all.
In the same way, the vast mass of giving of all the world
Is surpassed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who dedicates [all merit].
If a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, giving gifts to the world,

children.text: mamatāṃ na tatra karayenna ca vastuprema
children.translated_text: Does not create possessiveness there, nor attachment to objects—
Then his root of merit grows, of great power,
Like the moon's orb of light in the bright fortnight.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the thirty-first chapter, named The Chapter of <s>Dharmodgata</s> (<s>Dharmodgataparivarta</s>).
Through giving, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> cuts off the <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) destiny;
He cuts off poverty and likewise all afflictions.
He obtains endless, vast enjoyments while practicing,
And through giving, he matures beings who have fallen into hardship.
Through morality, he avoids the multiform animal destiny,

children.text: aṣṭau ca akṣaṇa kṣaṇāṃ labhate sa nityam
children.translated_text: And always obtains the opportune moment, [avoiding] the eight inopportune states.
Through patience, he obtains a form supremely noble—
Golden-complexioned, dear to the world, worth beholding.
Through energy, he does not undergo the loss of bright qualities;
He obtains endless knowledge, the treasury of the <s>Jinas</s>.
Through <s>dhyāna</s>, he abandons the sense-pleasures as loathsome,
[And] produces <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges), and achieves <s>samādhi</s>.
Through wisdom, having thoroughly understood the nature of <s>dharmas</s>,
He transcends the evil destinies to the end of the three realms.
Having turned the jewel-wheel of the bulls among men,
He teaches <s>Dharma</s> to the world for the extinction of suffering.
Having fulfilled these <s>dharmas</s>, that <s>Bodhisattva</s>
Also grasps the purification of fields and the purification of beings.
And one upholds the lineage of the <s>Buddha</s> and the lineage of the <s>Dharma</s>,
Likewise upholds the lineage of the <s>Saṃgha</s> and all dharmas.
The supreme physician in the world, healer of diseases—
The teaching of wisdom is declared to be the path to awakening.
By the name 'Accumulation of Precious Qualities' is this path to awakening;
Through this path, all beings attain it.
In the Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s>, the thirty-second chapter called 'Entrustment.'
Praise composed by <s>Ācārya Haribhadra</s>
To lead the world to the path bearing the stream of good fortune and happiness,
This was illuminated by the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, whose mind was established in compassion.
Having heard this <s>sūtra</s>, the abode of the truth of all dharmas, with devotion,
May those who have arrived, reaching that state, blow away their own impurities day and night.
In this age of confusion filled with many wrong views, when the recitation has gone far astray,
Having now seen the variant readings of the verses across many manuscripts, according to logic,
That which was purified by the noble one—a well for splitting the frontal lobes of the elephants of disputants—

children.text: lokārthaṃ hariṇā mayā suvihitā seyaṃ budhairgṛhyatām
children.translated_text: For the welfare of the world, this was well-arranged by me, <s>Hari</s>—may it be accepted by the wise.

children.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyā bhagavatyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ parivartānusāreṇa bhagavatī ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā samāptā //
children.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā</s> is completed, following the chapters of the Noble Blessed <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Those dharmas which arise from causes—the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that which is their cessation—thus speaks the great ascetic.
Praise by the scribe
He who recites the <s>Dharma</s> spoken by the <s>Sugata</s> out of devotion,
If somehow a syllable, word, verse-foot, or letter is deficient in measure,
Due to faults of the tongue, movements of breath, or the spread of phlegmatic defects—
O <s>Buddhas</s> dwelling in the excellent realms and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, please forgive!
Completed. Auspicious.
